tweets.text:
AI native teams will eventually force the surrounding organization to become AI native too.

Take software development. coding velocity is way up thanks to AI, while actual shipped products and business impact are unchanged in most companies. That’s cos the surrounding system of experimentation tooling, evaluation, launch processes, and gtm are outdated.

It’s like sticking a Ferrari engine in a sedan and racing it on Indian roads. The engine can rev faster but the car speed is limited by its system and environment.

AI native companies were built ground up for this new way of building and shipping. They’re also able to shed suboptimal processes faster.

Market forces will quickly force all companies to adapt or perish.

If you’re solving this for your company: map out your product lifecycle and rebuild it ground up - tooling, team structure, gtm, everything.

I asked Claude to populate a Civilization-style game map with real data from the US. Opus 5.5 downloaded and parse a ton of public data and 7 hours and 45K lines of code later... it works :)

- 31 real data sources including Census, BEA, BLS, EIA, NOAA, USGS, DoD, NPS, FAA, FEMA, CDC...
- Real elevation, land cover, GDP, jobs, power plants, mines, ports, airports, bases, parks, universities, freight flows, disasters; all reconciled onto one 25 km hex grid.
- The data is converted into Civilization language, e.g. Gold yield is GDP. A city's districts are its real industry specializations: San Jose gets a Campus, Detroit is "Motor city". Its citizens are its real workforce: 1 in 4 San Jose workers are engineers, coders or scientists, against 1 in 14 nationally. Wonders are chosen by published rules, such as national parks by visitor numbers and universities by R&D spending, etc etc.
- 19 lenses (income, degrees, faith, disasters…), a City View for 524 metros, and nine advisors plus an Explorer. The Explorer turns any column for any of 3,100+ counties into a table and scatter plot, linked to the map.
- Claude decided to skip a few states and territories sry
- Built using Claude Code desktop app, Opus 5.5 on medium and turning on ultracode.

It's deployed here: https://t.co/QMhmafXMj5 and the "?" has the source link too. I don't exactly know where I was going with this but it's really fun to browse and play with. 这轮熊市给出了两个相反的信号：按时间算，历次熊市走到这一步通常已经见底；按深度算，本轮从高点回撤约 53%，仍浅于以往的 77% 至 93%。

Thorn 现在盯着 58,525 美元。他表示，如果 BTC 日线收盘跌破这一价位，Galaxy 将视其为比特币开始向更低底部下探的信号。
首代卫星 AI1 展开后高 30 米、翼展 75 米，搭载 SpaceX 与英伟达联合设计的太空版 Vera Rubin NVL72，靠太阳能供电，在轨处理 AI 数据，再通过激光链路接入星链，把结果传回地面。 https://t.co/bLcWoF7eIV

马斯克要把 AI 数据中心搬上太空了。

据网传美国联邦通信委员会（@FCC）11 月 25 日公告，@SpaceX 获准部署最多 100 万颗轨道计算卫星，建设名为「Starmind」的太空数据中心星座，这也是美国历史上首次批准此类项目。

黄仁勋也是这一宏大计划的参与者。早在今年 8 月，英伟达就已宣布与 SpaceX 展开合作，为首代 Starmind 卫星打造适用于太空环境的 Vera Rubin NVL72 算力系统，利用太阳能供电，在轨完成 AI 计算，再通过激光链路接入星链，将计算结果传回地球。

为解决能源供应问题，SpaceX 还向德国设备商 Singulus 下单采购太阳能电池制造设备。据马斯克透露，对应年产能将达到 100 GW。他甚至将这一目标形容为打造一个「有意识的太阳」。

按照马斯克 @elonmusk 公布的时间表，首批卫星计划于 2027 年第四季度发射，2028 年扩大部署。

Current LLM meta feels special.

Gemini 4 Neon and Opus 5.5 are excellent, despite not being flagship models.

Neon is particularly surprising: up until this point Gemini models have always felt benchmaxxed and unusable for real work.

But Neon is great. I like its writing, it follows scope and instructions well, and its judgment (e.g. the recommendations it offers) is sound. 

It's the kind of model that you can ramble into and it will accurately derive your intent.

I don't get tired of using Neon, and the usual fog that I get after a long period of reading LLM outputs isn't there.

The usage limits for both Claude and Gemini subscriptions are also very generous.

It feels like nearly unlimited intelligence.

I'm using Opus 5.5 and 4 Neon as daily drivers. I like running them independently, but also getting them to work in parallel and check each other's work etc. This is both worthwhile and affordable given the current usage limits.

I'll still loop in Fable 5.2 for hard architectural work or to lift the fog when Neon/Opus get stuck in review loops, but this is rare. They tend to just get the job done.

This is a big change from just a few months ago, where it felt like if you weren't using the bigger/smartest models, you were missing out and were gonna get some dog shit outputs.

Very cool. Would recommend you give these models a spin.

Many people think LLMs suck because:

1. They tried them a while ago when models were far less capable

2. They used some instant model on a free plan and have never tried a frontier reasoning model

This is like complaining that consoles suck after trying a PS2 while the PS5 exists

That view was defensible maybe a year ago, but not anymore

You need to update ASAP

Heading into the end of November, Butler's closed beta has processed 41.7 billion tokens across 1.7 million model calls, and we're sharing its full capability map: every use case Butler handles today, placed by how complex the trade is, from a single asset to several venues and legs, and by how long Butler carries it out on its own, from a single execution to a strategy that runs around the clock.

The lower half of the map is largely in place. Butler executes from a single prompt without wallet setup or bridging, aggregates onchain, news and social signals before a decision, and manages positions on its own, mirroring within set limits, rebalancing to target weights and lining up exits when security news touches a holding.

The upper half is where most of the work has gone: structured trades, such as options protection priced across strikes and event bets paired with perp hedges, and systematic strategies that run quant specifications, trade macro releases as they print and work spreads between venues.

The next problem is speed. We're now tightening execution toward mid-frequency strategies, where seconds matter, and making a strategy something that can run for more than the one person who built it, with that person paid for sharing it.

We'll open a larger beta batch soon to test this together. Stay tuned.
